7.2.3 commercial utility deposits Mr. Hack.

Thank you, Madam Chair. This report is seeking an amendment to the water works by loss 7567 as well as the electrical light and power by law 2685 to allow for administrative discretion in applying commercial utility deposits.
As outlined in the report, the by law currently provides no discretion as to whether a two month utility deposit is required for commercial customers.
In completing a jurisdictional scan, the administration found that many utility providers do offer some level of discretion.
When a utility deposit is required.
While the use of deposits has grown in recent years to close off outstanding utility accounts, the administration is still recommending revisions to allow for administrative discretion.
When requiring deposits, which would include customer payment history with the city of Saskatoon.
If the account is signed up for direct debit and whether the account holder is the owner of the property.

If approved, the changes will bring Saskatoon more in line with other utility providers as well as recognize customers with good payment history while ensuring the city of Saskatoon is not exposed to a greater financial risk.
They're not expected to be any financial impacts to this change as requirements for the deposit will still continue to apply for the vast majority of account holders.
And exceptions to this will only be used in the most unlikely of default situations.

Consistent with the direction provided by City Council at its meeting on March 27th, the city owned sites are proposed to be offered to the market under a mix of market, non market, and no cost or nominal value list pricing.
Within the report and consistent with council direction, we have also noted the estimated financial implications for selling the parcels at non market pricing.

So given the goal of encouraging affordable units, the four properties would be offered publicly for a certain time period, and administration will request interested proponents to submit proposals for each site, which would be weighted against the criteria that we note on page three of the report.
So appendix one provides a brief overview of each of the city owned sites planned for release under the program, and the recommended approach for pricing the property.

2401 Broadway is proposed to be released at a market list price of 591,155 third avenue, the site kind of kitty quarter from city hall here, the civic parking lot is proposed to be released at a non market list price of just over 1.3 million.
Which represents a 50% discount of our estimate of fair market value.
25, 25th Street is also proposed to be released at a non market list price, this time $832,000, which is again a 50% discount from our estimate of fair market value.
And consistent with council direction, 1635 more culture would be offered at a nominal value or no cost.

While we're seeing the site being a desirable option for affordable housing, it will require additional reporting to committee and council as a bylaw is required to remove the minister reserve designation currently on the site.
This property would also require significant site preparation to relocate parking and existing community garden, which would not be impacted this year.
I would note that creating the site will have no impacts on current part programming and the active recreation in the area and cost for the site are proposed to be paid by the half funding.
So relevant financial applications for offering the sites at a discounted and nominal value are noted throughout the report.
